overview.summary: Financial analysts study financial information about companies, markets and projects to help organizations make decisions about money.
overview.problems: They estimate whether an investment or plan is likely to pay off, and track how a business is performing against its goals.
overview.worksWith: Finance and accounting teams, managers, investors, clients and bankers.
overview.workplaces: Banks, investment firms, company finance departments, consultancies, insurers and government bodies.

timeline.title: Check markets and news
timeline.description: The analyst reads overnight news and figures that may affect the company or its investments.
timeline.why: Prices and plans react to news.

timeline.title: Gathering and cleaning data
timeline.description: The analyst collects financial statements and market data in spreadsheets and checks them.
timeline.why: Wrong numbers lead to wrong decisions.

timeline.title: Building models and forecasts
timeline.description: The analyst builds spreadsheet models that estimate future income, costs and risks.

timeline.title: Checking assumptions
timeline.description: The analyst tests what happens if sales fall or costs rise.
timeline.why: Forecasts are uncertain, so ranges matter more than one number.

timeline.title: Writing a summary
timeline.description: The analyst turns the results into a short report or presentation with a clear recommendation and the risks.
timeline.why: Decision makers need clear, honest summaries.

timeline.title: Reporting season
timeline.description: Around quarter ends or results dates, hours can lengthen.
timeline.why: Reports are due on fixed dates.

challenges: Forecasts are uncertain and can be wrong.
Hours can be long around reporting deadlines.
The spreadsheet work is detailed and repetitive.
Decisions involving large amounts of money bring pressure.
Competition for entry roles is strong.
Strict ethical duties and conflict-of-interest rules apply.
workEnvironment: Mostly office based or remote, working on computers with spreadsheets and databases, often in teams. Hours are usually regular but can be long near deadlines. Some roles involve client meetings or travel.
rewards: Understanding how businesses and markets work
Skills that are useful in many industries
A mix of numbers and storytelling
tradeoffs: Pressure and long hours at busy times
Pay and opportunities that vary by country, firm and market conditions

activity.title: Compare two companies using public figures
steps: Choose two well-known companies in the same business, such as two phone makers or two shops.
Find their latest published yearly figures for sales and profit on their own investor pages or a trusted financial news site.
Put them in a spreadsheet and work out how much each grew compared with the year before.
Write three sentences on what the figures suggest and one thing the figures cannot tell you.
Note whether this kind of analysis felt interesting.
activity.outcome: You practise gathering figures, comparing them and being honest about their limits.
activity.safety: This is a learning exercise, not investment advice. Do not invest real money or share financial information about your family.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
